implementation_notes: An object holding a map is the registry, and Scala's collections supply the store: scala.collection.concurrent.TrieMap gives lock-free, thread-safe insert/lookup (with O(1) atomic snapshots for listing), while a plain mutable.Map plus synchronization is the simpler in-house variant. What replaces the classic Registry class is object + map + two methods; java.util.ServiceLoader remains available unchanged for cross-JAR discovery, though Scala objects cannot be instantiated by it, so a class proxy is needed when packaging a service. A class-based registry is justified when the registry should be injected as an explicit dependency instead of being global.
pitfalls: A plain mutable.Map is not thread-safe; use scala.collection.concurrent.TrieMap or synchronize, because the JVM will happily corrupt the map under concurrent registration.
TrieMap.putIfAbsent returns Option[Service] where Some means the key was already present - inverting that check is an easy, silent duplicate-policy bug.

object initialization is lazy and synchronized per class loader; two objects whose initializers touch each other can deadlock, and a registry initialized on first use may not be populated when another object's initializer needs it.
Kotlin-style caveat applies to Scala as well: ServiceLoader needs a public no-arg constructor, so an object cannot be a directly declared provider.
